svg.title: Agent Path evaluation and vertex-to-vertex movement
svg.desc: Nine linked flowcharts show generic route planning, directed edge evaluation, waypoint approach, resource admission, control operation, transport and chamber journeys, movement and commit, and recovery. Function and source links refer to this repository. Diamonds are inline decisions unless identified as predicate functions. Dashed arrows indicate cross-panel calls or next-tick continuation, not synchronous calls.

text.tspan: General decision logic for any Path — not an example route. Read A, then follow the lettered, clickable subchart ports.
Blue = function/action • Amber diamond = predicate or enclosing-function [inline] condition • Green = linked subchart/continuation • Red = refusal/recovery
SC = SimulationCoordinator. World forwards traversal APIs to SC. Source references are clickable relative links; regenerate after code changes.
Solid arrows show local control flow. Dashed arrows show tick continuation or subchart handoff. A subchart return resumes its caller; preparation never grants admission.
Scope: autonomous Path following. Player input-specific movement is intentionally not expanded. Panels summarize function-level branches, not every defensive guard.
Planning produces route intent. Every movement transition still follows the request → allocation → permit → commit

A physical Interactable waypoint blocks skipping for Arms/None, but Remote control may omit a control-only detour. Gap,
threshold, mount/body and Local-depth constraints still apply. Early queue stopping takes precedence over Door crossing-band
arrival. An absent/finished Path idles instead of creating a request.
Agent::allocateTraversal() rechecks before starting, not in the middle of an admitted crossing. Every branch

gates. Extensible passage repeats Permission adherence even when extended. Fully open standalone Bulkhead Doors allow
concurrent bidirectional passage; controlled Door crossing lanes remain coordinated.
Device activation and physical crossing are separate. Remote control still uses control ownership, authorization,

Manual ordinary Doors have no separate Button: activateRemoteAnticipatoryInteraction() can issue eligible OpenDoor directly;
E handles physical threshold operation. No eligible target means continue Path movement, not automatically fail.
Panel/BoothWindow ownership-specific eligibility exists, but neither creates a passage edge.
Source/target Sector selects boarding, riding or exit. This panel is called from E for every corresponding journey

g.title: SC::allocateLiftDisembarking(): Reserve safe exit; walk within car/carriage as needed; retain occupancy until crossing commit. Committed exits survive later authorization loss.

g.title: SC::allocateAirlockTraversal(): Alternative Airlock branch: entry control/shared accepted call, entry/exit clearance, same-side batch capacity, interlocked Door admission.

text.tspan: Alternative Airlock branch: entry control/shared accepted call, entry/exit

g.title: SC::allocateSecurityScannerTraversal(): Alternative Chamber branch: fixed entry/exit, exit fit and Location access; automatic capacity-one Scanner or batched Decontamination.

text.tspan: Alternative Chamber branch: fixed entry/exit, exit fit and Location access;

a.title: SC::grantTraversalRequest(): Each journey leg grants only when ready. Airlock/Chamber close–process–open progression is resource-owned; return E/H for physical commit.

text.tspan: Each journey leg grants only when ready. Airlock/Chamber close–process–open
progression is resource-owned; return E/H for physical commit.
g7 and g8 are independent entries from E, not stages after a Lift. Vehicle rides and entry/exit are separate requests.
Platform contiguous Lift legs form one final-Stop journey; Shuttle carriage/door assignment is coordinated. Interrupted or
Broken journeys use safe-exit recovery in I, never teleportation.
Runtime movement preserves physical source membership until a valid authorized commit; source and target may
coincide in 2D but lie on different Layers.

g.title: Agent::allocateTraversal(): Adopt Granted permit; record accepted exit pose, coalesce contiguous platform legs, and apply permitted waypoint skipping.

text.tspan: Adopt Granted permit; record accepted exit pose, coalesce contiguous
platform legs, and apply permitted waypoint skipping.

g.title: SC::commitTraversal() [inline]: Request/permit live, owner matched, endpoint or in-place rule and reservations/sector/interlocks valid?

a.title: I · Commit not accepted: Stay AwaitingTraversalCommit; cleanup handles timeout/expiry. Never transfer without authority.
Agent::commitTraversal(): Commit sector/occupancy transfer; consume node(s) via nextPathNode(); syncPoseToSector(); cleanup releases ownership → D or arrival A.

text.tspan: Commit sector/occupancy transfer; consume node(s) via nextPathNode();
syncPoseToSector(); cleanup releases ownership → D or arrival A.
h1 is a threshold-only step; other edge types proceed to h2. Bulkhead crossing is physical horizontal movement, ordinary Door
crossing is timed in place. Waiting Agents move only toward resource-owned local goals or remote-range approach targets.
Crossings finish in their admitted pose even if later conditions change.
Continuation paths are conditional: waiting does not mean immediate failure, and replanning does not revoke an

Pending; local-goal retries may deny LocalGoalUnreachable.

a.title: D · Resume valid Path: assignPath(); active movement resumes on following tick.

g.title: SC::updateMovementGoals(): Publish RouteLost once. Cancellation/target removal emits its appropriate outcome; behaviour may choose another destination.

text.tspan: Publish RouteLost once. Cancellation/target removal emits its appropriate
outcome; behaviour may choose another destination.
i3 and i5 are independent refusal/preparation entries as well as recovery gates; voluntary planning need not pass through
remote Door retries. Paused simulation freezes planning intervals. Inactive Agents do not walk or press. Safe committed
completion is an exception for that journey, never permission for a new admission.
